items.prompt:
In the question below, some statements are given followed by two conclusions. Take the statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, and decide which of the conclusions logically follows.

**Statements:**
Only a few pens are rings.
All rings are coins.
No coin is a lamp.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some pens are not lamps.
II. All pens being rings is a possibility.

steps: I. Some pens are not lamps — **follows**: the pens that are rings are coins, and no coin is a lamp, so those pens are certainly not lamps.
II. All pens being rings is a possibility — **does not follow**: "Only a few pens are rings" already says some pens are not rings, so all pens can never be rings.
Hence only I follows.
solution.shortcut: "Only a few A are B" = Some A are B + Some A are not B. So "All A are B" (or "All A being B is a possibility") is always false, while "All A can never be B" and "Some A are not B" always follow.
solution.trap: Reading "only a few" as plain "some" makes II look possible — but "only a few" also fixes that some pens lie outside rings.
